subject: Object Oriented Programming

questions.markdown: Analyze how primitive and non-primitive (reference) data types differ in Java with respect to memory allocation, assignment behavior, and comparison operations. Use examples to illustrate how these differences can affect program logic, performance, and debugging.
Write a Java program that demonstrates the use of all eight primitive data types. Initialize each type with a sample value, and show at least one example of type casting between compatible types.

Analyse the structural and behavioral differences between interfaces and abstract classes in Java. Compare their use cases and evaluate how enhancements in Java 8 and later-such as default and static methods-impact interface design. Use examples to illustrate how these features influence code architecture and flexibility

Write a Java program that defines an interface Payment with a method processPayment(double amount). Create two classes, CreditCard and UPI, that implement Payment and provide their own logic for processing payments. In the main method, create objects of both classes and call processPayment() with sample amounts.
Write a short Java program where two threads attempt to update a shared counter without synchronization, and then modify it to use a synchronized method to ensure thread safety.

Discuss the following for writing exception handling code in Java.

- Catching specific exceptions vs generic ones
- Avoiding empty catch blocks
- Using finally for resource cleanup
- Logging exceptions effectively
- When to use custom exceptions

Support your answer with suitable examples.
Write a generic method printArray() that takes an array of any type and prints its elements. Demonstrate the method with arrays of Integer, String, and Double.

Analyse the structure and component interaction in a JavaFX program that extends the Application class. Break down how Label, StackPane, and Scene work together to render a window titled 'My First JavaFX App' with the message 'Welcome to JavaFX!'. Use a code snippet to illustrate how these elements contribute to the overall GUI layout and lifecycle.

CERT recommends avoiding expressions with side effects in conditional statements. Explain why using assignments or method calls that modify state inside if, while, or for conditions can lead to unpredictable behavior.

Apply the concept of encapsulation by designing a Java class that protects its data using access modifiers and getter/setter methods. Use a real-world analogy to guide your design and demonstrate how encapsulation supports modularity and data protection through a relevant example.
